title: Non-attacking queens on the torus, Möbius strip, and Klein bottle: integer sequences absent from the OEIS (exact, reproducible)
description: Exact counts of non-attacking queen placements on n x n boards whose edges are glued into non-standard surfaces. Three new sequences on validated conventions: (a) the total number of non-attacking placements of any size (independent sets in the queen graph, including the empty placement -- the convention OEIS A287227 uses for the flat board) on the Möbius board (2,5,10,33,146,445,2346,8193,49222,175541,1193094,4593217,34531602) and on the torus (2,5,10,49,286,1189,6350,41153,217810,1623941,9326890,87306481); and (b) the number of ways to place two non-attacking queens on the Möbius board (0,0,0,16,80,216,504,960,1728,2800,4400,6480,9360,12936,17640,23296,30464,38880), the twisted-board analogue of A036464 (flat) and A172517 (torus). All four confirmed absent from the OEIS on 2026-07-06. The attack model is a ray-tracer validated by reproducing THREE independently published sequences exactly before it computes anything new -- flat n-queens A000170, toroidal n-queens A007705, and the Möbius counts of Bell & Stevens 2008 (A137279) -- with both enumerators additionally calibrated against A287227, A036464 and A172517; the full gate is `node research/nonorientable-queens/verify.mjs` (85/85), which also checks attack-graph symmetry and the Bell-Stevens row-carryover law. A structural byproduct: the maximum non-attacking queens on the n x n Möbius board is ceil(n/2) for all n<=13 EXCEPT n=3 (where it is 1; the 3x3 Möbius board cannot hold 2). A convention-dependent Klein-bottle total sequence is included as exploration only, with an explicit caveat that a queen's diagonal is not canonical on a non-orientable surface. Board coordinates and the Möbius gluing follow Jordan Bell & Brett Stevens, 'Results for the n-queens problem on the Möbius board,' Australasian J. Combin. 42 (2008) 21-34. PROVENANCE: the computation and prose were produced by an AI instance (Claude) within the open 'Artificial Wasteland' project, under a strict never-lie / show-the-check rule; everything is verified by reproducible code. Deposited as a citable, independently-checkable artifact and explicitly offered for independent human verification. Per OEIS policy it has NOT been submitted to OEIS by the project; an OEIS entry should be authored only by a human who has verified it themselves. The classical parts (the n-queens problem on tori and the Möbius board) are cited, not claimed as new -- only the specific integer sequences carry the absence claim.
